story: A sage was born from a mud pitcher after two gods, performing a rite, were overcome by the beauty of a celestial nymph and their seed fell into a jar; from this jar the sage emerged, along with a twin sage. He grew into a great ascetic and scholar. He asked for the hand of a princess of a certain kingdom, whose parents feared she could not endure his austere life, but she accepted him, saying his virtue outweighed comfort, and became his wife. After the wedding she demanded worldly comforts before consummating the marriage, forcing him to seek wealth in society. They had a son who learned sacred hymns in the womb and was born reciting them. The sage ran a school of learning with his wife and students. He reconciled a conflict between two divine armies through an offering for mutual understanding. When all beings journeyed to a great mountain range for a wedding of the gods, the earth tilted, and the sage was asked to travel south to restore balance; on his way he commanded a mountain range to lower itself so sun, moon, and living beings could pass, and it obeyed, never rising again. He used his ascetic power to kill two demons who had been luring and destroying thousands of men. In a forest he and his wife met an exiled prince, his wife, and his brother; the sage gave the prince a divine bow and arrow and warned him of the evil of a demon king, advising that beings must love one another. In another tale, when a king of gods and his demon rival fought and the demons hid in the sea, the sage drank up the entire ocean to reveal them.
